business_problem: The ICO registration team receives high volumes of email queries, and manually reading and responding to each one takes time, can create high caseloads and risks backlogs and delayed responses.
solution_summary: The ICO uses a Naïve Bayes classifier to inspect incoming registration-inbox email text and identify requests to change a business address. The model was trained on emails collected from that inbox; email headers are removed before machine-learning text classification, and training-data access was restricted to ICS.AI personnel working in an ICO-managed environment. The source says the model was created from Azure Database and that training data was deleted from that database afterward; original emails remain in the registration inbox for 12 months. In production, only classifications with 80% certainty of an address-change request trigger an automated reply linking to the online change-of-address service and explaining information needed to process the request. Other incorrectly classified emails receive a default acknowledgement. ICS.AI was contracted to develop the algorithm with Microsoft. The record does not identify the production hosting, email platform, or integration mechanism.

solution_components.name: Naïve Bayes classifier
solution_components.role: Classifies registration-inbox email content to identify business address-change requests.

solution_components.name: Azure Database
solution_components.role: Held training data used to create the model, which was deleted from the database after model creation.

data_flow: Emails sent to the ICO registration inbox provided training data; email headers are removed before text classification. In production, the classifier assesses incoming email content. When it identifies an address-change request with 80% certainty, an automated reply links to the online change-of-address service; other cases receive a default acknowledgement.
business_outcome: The tool sifts out some address-change emails and redirects customers to self-service, helping avoid backlogs and giving Data Protection Fees Officers more capacity to handle complex requests and respond in a timely manner.
architecture_clues: Original registration-inbox emails remain for 12 months; training data was deleted from Azure Database after model creation

evidence_quotes: The classification model uses a Naïve Bayes classifier to determine the context of a request.
The tool classifies approximately 23,000 emails a month.
Only emails with an 80% certainty of a change of address request will be sent an email containing the link to the change of address form.
The algorithm was developed by ICS.AI and Microsoft.
Training data was deleted after the model was created from the Azure Database while the original email will remain in the registration inbox for 12 months.
